text:
I got my RTX 3070 FE for MSRP and I love it. The 3080 FE wasn't even close to being back in stock it seemed which ended up being true for awhile. 
But honestly then i would of had to upgrade my PSU and maybe even some other things so I wasn't too worried..

Anyway the $500 price for the RTX3070 FE is really good. Its an amazing 1440p and light 4K gaming GPU. Super quiet. Runs cool all the time and i have it OC'd with Afterburner and it hits 1910-1925MHZ now at 99%.
I can play any new game like Halo Inf, Forza H5, and more with a mixture of High, Med, & Ultra settings. I get 120+fps on basically all the regular games. 
It blows away my Series X and i just really like playing on the PC, even though I refuse to anything but a controller to play lol.
Id highly recommend just getting the 3070 if you have a 1440p monitor especially. You dont have to deal the very high VRAM Temps on the RTX3080 FE & up. It needs the thermal pads replaced basically as soon as you get it because the GDDR6X memory will hit 100+ in the hotspot areas.. 
Plus its really alittle but of overkill for what you need for a setup like that. 

The 3070 can do it all with maybe a few less frames, but with a smaller Card and almost Half the Power Draw and heat buildup..

text: *Me a grizzled veteran of the PC wasteland in 2021, scared, forlorn, missing an eye, perched on my hillside savaged by the biting winds.  I look into the distance, the bleak twilight playing across a vast rusty plain, dust rises on the horizon, my lone eye squints.  "Bots, scalper bots, an army of them, they smell GPUs, and blood."  Quickly I mount my scrappy motorbike, an I7 960 thumps in protest finally belching a cloud of smoke roaring into begrudging life.  The miles of the plains rattle under salvaged wheels, finally I join the host.  I see other scrappers, their machines all aged and worn.  We might parley, but for our haste, all cooperation ceases in the mad rush.  Just behind the host of bots now, their bestial machine legs and vicious hunger force us to keep a weary distance.  I hear cries from behind me, indistinguishable at first, but finally a discernible word forces me to look behind me, "MINER!".  Behind the ravenous host a moving mountain strides at impossible speed, smoke belching from its myriad stacks giving the impression of a volcano with spider legs.  The effort now one of desperation the site of the GPU drop lies just ahead.  First the bots swarm the haphazard heap of boxes, a few scrappers managing to grab hold of a GPU, only to have it clawed out of their carts by greasy iron claws.  I pull away from the madness playing out beside me, I know it is already to late.  The ground heaves as the boxes and some of the bots are inhaled by a gaping maw, the Miner consumes a massive chunk of the desolation indiscriminately chewing the very earth to feed the mighty fires in its metal belly.  I look for another hillside to camp on, tomorrow is another day, at least I survived this drop...

text:
Sigh. Well that was yet another disappointment. And before you flame me know that I live in NZ. And the promise of more powerful GPUs and NVIDIA hitting the reset button on pricing really excited us here.

Only those reduced prices amounted to nothing here. In fact, here in NZ prices are increasing steadily with every new release. The 3070 launched here this morning and the lowest price is $1099. That's $200 more than the cheapest 2070 at launch, and a whopping $448 more than the cheapest GTX 1070 at launch. Worse they didn't tell us the prices in advance and made us queue up outside stores for a 3am launch. I imagine more than a few gamers ended up buying a 3070 at these prices just because they'd waited in line all night and didn't want to feel like they'd wasted that time.

I guess I'm waiting to see what effect AMD's new kit has on the market...

text:
@logan2906  Economic laws, as well as logic and reason doesn't suddenly change when the object we're discussing changes. The same rules apply to apples, oranges, cars and theatre tickets. As well as medicine, healthcare, housing and clothing. The importance of the object is not a factor. 

My definition of morality starts at looking where force, coercion or aggression is applied. Stealing an apple is immoral since you're taking it without consent. Offering your apple for sale in a market place is not immoral since you're not forcing anyone to do anything. There are certainly more layers than this but the basic, most important one is to NOT use aggression. Then we can talk.  

Now, the insulin case is no different. A high demand with a low supply on a market can only lead to higher prices, there is no way around it. You can force low prices (immoral) but that would just lead to shortages and people will still be left without and since you're messing up market signals to produce more (no incentives to supply) the shortages would be much worse than if you simply had allowed prices to rise to market levels.

Your specific hypothetical scenario would not be unethical but practically impossible since you can't simply buy an entire stock like that. Given a true market situation with free pricing they would up the price instantly when you try to do that making you pay 10x on the latter half. Now you have an expensive inventory and you're competing with 1000 other suppliers for market share. It's impossible for you to win there. That's why companies don't do this. This is why it's so important to learn basic economics because most people think this is a likely scenario but in reality it's utterly impossible. 

But we should also note that often in the medical field you don't have a free market (most people vehemently refuse to allow it) and therefore you will have artificial shortages and skewed incentives for the players involved. Taxes and politicians do that, every time. And like clock work those government induced problems are always blamed on "the free market" and the left uses it to trick people to vote for them and promises "high quality health care to everyone". The resulting situation however is just messing the system up further with more government regulations, skewed incentives, shortages and poor outcomes.

I strongly recommend Thomas Sowell - Basic Economics if you want to learn more about this type of thinking. It's an area where most people think they know how stuff works but in reality it's often exactly the opposite. Quite fascinating subject.

Hey, I haven't been a fan of the channel super long, but within the last year or so, I've really gotten into pc building and such, I built my own, as well as a couple for some other friends. @askkutay  The dollar has increased in value alot the past 5 years.

We went from about 6 kroner per dollar, too about 9 kroner per dollar now.

Its cause during 2008 financial crisis, US printed alot of money. So did most other nations. But after the crisis was over, US started to take back dollars from circulation. Thus increasing dollar value. While most nations did nothing.

And you have your president who makes your currency very unstable with him playing a semi crazy on the international scene. That usualy scares investors out of Turkey. So money is worth less when all the money is fleeing the country incase your president gets himself into real trouble with the international community. 

Cause its hard to get money out of a nation once they are under embargo or in war etc.

text:
For real, the 3080 has been out for over a month now. How is it literally impossible to find any available stock anywhere? Do factories not produce around the clock? Do cargo ships not leave the harbours every other day? Even with a months delay, I would've expected the second, hopefully much larger shipment of stock, the one that actual consumers were gonna buy, to have arrived by now. 

If you type in RTX 3080 or RTX 3090 into Amazon NONE of the results are even relevant to the new generation. It's all 2000 series cards and various misplaced accesories. What the hell. Even Nvidias own wesbite does not list a single availability. What a shame, and what a marketing fiasco for NVIDIA. Imagine any other consumer industry in which a product launches and you lose out on a huge amount of inital sales, because you didn't plan your supply amount properly. Finance people and investors would have your ass beaten.

This gives me little hope for the 3070. The real question is not if they underestimated the demand all the rave reviews of the 3000 series would generate for the 3070, but rather to which order of magnitude they did.
